newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Hume interested in Irish presidency - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Hume interested in Irish presidency - newspaper.

text.p: Northern Ireland peace broker John Hume is seriously considering standing for the Presidency of Ireland when Mary Robinson steps down in September, according to a report in the New York Times.
It quoted Hume, a moderate Catholic Irish nationalist, as saying that Ireland's main political parties had approached him about standing for the job and he was "tending towards accepting the offer".

Hume, a member of the British parliament, European assembly and tireless promoter of his native Londonderry, Northern Ireland's second city, was on retreat on the Scottish island of Iona and not available for comment.

He has in the past played down speculation that he might stand for the position because of the role his Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP) is playing in Northern Ireland peace talks, which enter a critical phase in September.
The New York Times, whose interview was published by the Irish Times, quoted Hume as saying: "I would be a super salesman for Ireland, trying to bring investment and jobs here."

It was the first time the 60-year-old peace campaigner had been quoted as being positive about his nomination for the Irish presidency, a job which had a largely ceremonial role until Robinson took over in 1990.
She is to stand down next month to become the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights after injecting a new sense of pride and direction to Irishness at home and abroad.

Other women's names being touted as her successor include that of Dana, a devout Catholic singer, opposition politicians Mary Banotti and Avril Doyle and Maire Geoghegan-Quinn, a former justice minister of the ruling Fianna Fail party.
Dana, whose real name is Rosemary Brown, has been put forward by the pro-life lobby. She became famous in 1970 when she won the Eurovision Song Contest.
Former Prime Minister Albert Reynolds has also expressed interest in the job and October 30 has been set as the date for an election, if one is held.

But if all political parties agreed on Hume's nomination, an election would not be held and Hume would succeed a woman of whom former Prime Minister John Bruton said: "Mary Robinson is the best president Ireland ever had."

Hume's health and workload have been of considerable concern to colleagues within the SDLP and outside for several years. He spends his life travelling between Ireland, America, Britain and European parliamentary sessions.
He was instrumental in brokering a ceasefire in August 1994 by the Irish Republican Army (IRA) guerrillas to their war against British rule of Northern Ireland.

The ceasefire collapsed in February last year and was restored on July 20, paving the way for the IRA's political wing, Sinn Fein, to join the SDLP and represent Northern Ireland's Catholic minority at the Belfast peace talks.
